unit.title: Plans & invitations
canDo: Say what you are going to do this weekend

lessons.title: This weekend
lessons.goal: Talk about weekend plans with time words and outdoor places

lessons.title: Will you, shall we
lessons.goal: Use -(으)ㄹ 거예요 for plans and -(으)ㄹ까요? for suggestions, then add -(으)세요

lessons.title: A table for four
lessons.goal: Follow a phone reservation and catch the time, the seats and the order

lessons.title: My weekend plan
lessons.goal: Read a plan for the weekend and find what happens, why and when

lessons.title: Make a plan, invite a friend
lessons.goal: Plan, suggest, invite and explain a reason without hints

grammar.label: going to (-(으)ㄹ 거예요)
grammar.explanation: Add -(으)ㄹ 거예요 to a verb stem for a plan or a future fact: 갈 거예요, 먹을 거예요. Use it for real plans, not for what is happening right now.

examples.en: I'm going to go hiking this weekend.
I'm going to watch a movie next week.

grammar.label: shall we? (-(으)ㄹ까요?)
grammar.explanation: Use -(으)ㄹ까요? to ask 'shall we…?' or to wonder 'should I…?'. The answer is usually 네, 좋아요 or 아니요, 힘들어요.

examples.en: Shall we go to a restaurant for lunch?

grammar.label: because (-아/어서)
grammar.explanation: Use -아/어서 when the first clause is the reason: 시간이 없어서 늦을 거예요. The tense is not added here, and a second 그래서 is not needed.

examples.en: I'll be late because I have no time.
There won't be seats because there are a lot of people.

grammar.mistake: 없어서 그래서 ✗ (one reason is enough) → 없어서 ✓

grammar.label: please do (-(으)세요)
grammar.explanation: Attach -(으)세요 to a verb stem to ask someone politely to do something: 주문하세요, 기다리세요. It is also the everyday honorific ending.

examples.en: Please look at the menu and order.

sentences.english: I'm going to go hiking this weekend.
sentences.literal: This weekend, hiking go-will.
distractors: I went hiking this weekend.
I'm going to go hiking next weekend.
I'm not going to go hiking this weekend.
sentences.notes: 등산을 가다 is the fixed phrase: 'go hiking', not 등산을 하다 alone.

sentences.english: The day after tomorrow I'm going to take photos in the park.
sentences.literal: As for the day after tomorrow, in the park photos take-will.
distractors: I'm going to take photos at the beach the day after tomorrow.
I took photos in the park last week.
I'm going to take photos in the park tomorrow.
sentences.notes: 찍다 is used for photos; 사진을 찍어요 = take a photo.

sentences.korean: 다음 주에 영화관에서 영화를 볼 거예요.
sentences.romanization: daeum jue yeonghwagwaneseo yeonghwareul bol geoyeyo.
sentences.english: Next week I'm going to watch a movie at the cinema.
sentences.literal: Next week, at the cinema, a movie watch-will.
distractors: I'm going to watch a movie at home next week.
I'm going to watch a play at the cinema next week.
I'm not going to watch a movie next week.
sentences.notes: 보다 has no final consonant before the ending, so the ㄹ is added directly: 보 + ㄹ = 볼.

sentences.english: I'm going to go camping at the sea.
sentences.literal: At the sea, camping do-will.
distractors: I'm going to go camping in the mountains.
I went camping at the sea.
I'm not going to go camping at the sea.
sentences.notes: 캠핑을 하다 = go camping; 하다 keeps its 했 form in the past but not here.

sentences.english: On the weekend I'm going to go up the mountain.
sentences.literal: On the weekend, up the mountain go-up-will.
distractors: I'm going to go up the mountain next month.
I'm going to go down the mountain on the weekend.
I'm not going to go up the mountain on the weekend.
sentences.notes: Korean says 'go up' with 올라가다; the place takes 에.

sentences.english: I'm going to make a plan this week.
sentences.literal: This week, a plan make-will.
distractors: I made a plan last week.
I'm going to make a plan next month.
I'm not going to make a plan this week.
sentences.notes: 계획을 세우다 is the natural verb: 'to set a plan'.

sentences.english: Shall we go to a restaurant for lunch?
sentences.literal: For lunch, to a restaurant go-shall?
distractors: Shall we go to a cafe for lunch?
Did we go to a restaurant for lunch?
I'm going to go to a restaurant for lunch.
sentences.notes: 갈까요? asks for the other person's opinion, so both people are included.

sentences.korean: 제 생일 파티에 꼭 올 거예요?
sentences.romanization: je saengil patie kkok ol geoyeyo?
sentences.english: Are you definitely coming to my birthday party?
sentences.literal: To my birthday party, surely come-will?
distractors: Are you coming to my birthday dinner?
Did you come to my birthday party?
I'm coming to your birthday party.
sentences.notes: With a rising tone, -(으)ㄹ 거예요? asks about the other person's plan.

sentences.english: I'll prepare the cake.
sentences.literal: As for the cake, I prepare-will.
distractors: I will buy the cake.
You will prepare the cake.
I prepared the cake.
sentences.notes: 제가 marks 'I' as the doer, which answers 'who?'. The subject marker 가 goes after 제.

sentences.english: Shall we buy the gift together?
sentences.literal: As for the gift, together buy-shall?
distractors: Shall we buy the gift alone?
Shall we buy the flowers together?
We bought the gift together.
sentences.notes: 함께 and 같이 both mean 'together'; 함께 is a little more formal.

sentences.english: I'll wait at the restaurant.
sentences.literal: At the restaurant, wait-will.
distractors: I'll wait at the cinema.
I waited at the restaurant.
I won't wait at the restaurant.
sentences.notes: 기다리다 has no final consonant, so 기다리 + ㄹ = 기다릴.

sentences.english: I'll call at lunchtime.
sentences.literal: At lunch, a phone call do-will.
distractors: I'll call in the evening.
I called at lunchtime.
I won't call at lunchtime.
sentences.notes: 전화하다 = make a phone call; 전화할 거예요 = I'll call.

sentences.english: Please reserve dinner in advance.
sentences.literal: As for dinner, in advance reserve-please.
distractors: Please reserve lunch.
I reserved dinner.
Please don't reserve dinner.
sentences.notes: 예약하다 takes -(으)세요 when you are telling someone politely to book: 예약하세요.

sentences.english: What time will you arrive?
sentences.literal: At what time arrive-will?
distractors: What time did you arrive?
Where will you arrive?
What time will you leave?
sentences.notes: 몇 시에 asks the clock time; 도착하다 is to arrive at a place.

sentences.english: There won't be any seats on the weekend.
sentences.literal: On the weekend, seats not-exist-will.
distractors: There will be seats on the weekend.
There are no seats today.
There will be a lot of people on the weekend.
sentences.notes: 없다 becomes 없을 거예요; the subject takes 가 because 자리 ends in a vowel.

sentences.english: I'll be late because I have no time.
sentences.literal: Time not-exist-because, late-will.
distractors: I'll be late because I have time.
I'll be early because I have no time.
I was late because I had no time.
sentences.notes: -아/어서 gives the reason and is never followed by 그래서 in the same sentence.

sentences.english: Shall we look at the menu and order?
sentences.literal: Menu look-and, order-shall?
distractors: Shall we order without looking at the menu?
Shall we pay and look at the menu?
We looked at the menu and ordered.
sentences.notes: -고 chains the two actions and only the last one carries 까요.

sentences.english: Shall we go to this restaurant next time?
sentences.literal: Next time, to this restaurant go-shall?
distractors: Shall we go to this restaurant today?
Shall we go to the cinema next time?
We went to this restaurant last time.
sentences.notes: 이 식당 = this restaurant; 다음에 = next time, not 'next week'.

sentences.english: On the weekend I'm going to ride a bike in the park.
sentences.literal: On the weekend, in the park, a bicycle ride-will.
distractors: I'm going to ride a bike at the beach on the weekend.
I rode a bike in the park on the weekend.
I'm not going to ride a bike on the weekend.
sentences.notes: 타다 is used for bikes, buses and trains: 자전거를 타요.

sentences.english: School vacation will start next month.
sentences.literal: As for vacation, next month start-will.
distractors: School vacation will start next week.
School vacation ended last month.
School vacation will start next year.
sentences.notes: 시작하다 is a 하다 verb, so it follows the same future shape: 시작할 거예요.

sentences.english: Get a good rest during vacation.
sentences.literal: During vacation, deeply rest-please.
distractors: Get a good rest during the semester.
Study hard during vacation.
Don't rest during vacation.
sentences.notes: 푹 쉬세요 is the everyday phrase for 'get a proper rest'.

sentences.english: I'm going to make a schedule and then exercise.
sentences.literal: A schedule make-because, exercise do-will.
distractors: I'm going to make a schedule and study.
I made a schedule and exercised.
I'm going to exercise without a schedule.
sentences.notes: -아/어서 can also mean 'do A and then B' when the two steps are close together.

sentences.english: On Saturday evening I'm going to eat at a good restaurant.
sentences.literal: On weekend evening, at a good restaurant eat-will.
distractors: I'm going to eat at home on Saturday evening.
I ate at a good restaurant on the weekend.
I'm going to eat at a good restaurant on Wednesday evening.
sentences.notes: 맛집 literally means a 'taste house' - a restaurant people recommend.

sentences.korean: 일요일에는 아무 계획이 없어요. 그래서 집에서 쉴 거예요.
sentences.romanization: iryoireneun amu gyehoeki eopseoyo. geuraeseo jibeseo swil geoyeyo.
sentences.english: I have no plans on Sunday. So I'm going to rest at home.
sentences.literal: On Sunday, any plan does-not-exist. So, at home rest-will.
distractors: I have a lot of plans on Sunday. So I'm going to rest at home.
I have no plans on Sunday. So I'm going to work at home.
I had no plans on Sunday. So I rested at home.
sentences.notes: 아무 needs a negative verb: 아무 계획이 없어요 = I have no plans at all.

dialogue.title: A table for four
dialogue.setting: A phone call to reserve a table for dinner.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Hello. I'd like to reserve a table for tonight.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Sure. What time will you come?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ko: 일곱 시에 갈 거예요. 네 명이에요.
lines.rom: ilgop si-e gal geoyeyo. ne myeongieyo.
lines.en: I'll come at seven. There are four of us.

lines.speaker: A
lines.en: Can I order from the menu by phone?

lines.speaker: A
lines.ko: 좋아요. 그럼 파스타 두 개를 주문할 거예요.
lines.rom: joayo. geureom paseuta du gaereul jumunhal geoyeyo.
lines.en: Good. Then I'll order two pastas.

lines.speaker: B
lines.en: Yes, we'll be waiting at seven.

reading.title: My weekend plan
reading.ko: 이번 주말은 아주 바쁠 거예요. 토요일 아침에는 수영을 할 거예요. 점심에는 친구와 맛집에 갈 거예요. 사람이 많을 거예요. 오후에는 공원에서 자전거를 탈 거예요. 저녁에는 집에서 영화를 볼 거예요. 일요일에는 아무 계획이 없어요. 그래서 푹 쉴 거예요. 일요일 밤에는 일찍 잘 거예요. 다음 달에는 방학이 시작돼요. 방학에는 제주도에 갈 거예요. 아주 즐거울 거예요.
reading.en: This weekend is going to be very busy. On Saturday morning I'm going to swim. At lunch I'm going to a good restaurant with a friend. There will be a lot of people. In the afternoon I'm going to ride a bike in the park. In the evening I'm going to watch a movie at home. On Sunday I have no plans. So I'm going to rest properly. On Sunday night I'm going to go to bed early. Next month school vacation starts. During vacation I'm going to Jeju Island. It's going to be a lot of fun.

questions.q: What will the writer do on Saturday morning?
questions.why: 토요일 아침에는 수영을 할 거예요 = On Saturday morning I'm going to swim.

questions.q: Why will the writer rest on Sunday?
questions.why: 일요일에는 아무 계획이 없어요. 그래서 푹 쉴 거예요.

questions.q: Where will the writer go during vacation?
questions.why: 방학에는 제주도에 갈 거예요 = During vacation I'm going to Jeju Island.
